name: describe_migration_instrument
note: INSTRUMENT DESCRIPTION (code-verified backtest/migration.py + campaign.py:460-467 + config.yaml:110-112; prerequisite to the cascade-decay proposal — answered before design). RUNG SET: the six ladder TFs [1min,3min,5min,15min,30min,1h], ADJACENT pairs only (1->3,3->5,5->15,15->30,30->1h). MIGRATION EVENT on child->parent, three clauses: (a) PERSISTENCE = >=2 (min_child_labels) same-direction STRUCTURAL child labels closing within the parent bar's open window (child ts in (parent_close - parent_TF, parent_close]; a single child label never counts); (b) parent bar closes with a same-direction structural label; (c) RECRUITMENT = parent rel_volume >= 1.2 (recruitment_floor) vs the parent's own session-time bin — participation must expand at the parent; recruited is a bool, margin recorded. CHAIN: consecutive rungs, matching direction, previous-rung event inside the current parent-TF window; chain_rungs = max(prev)+1. STUDY: per-segment drift-adjusted forward excess at 5/10/20 SIGNAL bars after chain events, evaluated only for chain events landing on the 15M signal grid (off-grid counted, dropped); groups = chain_rungs x recruited x segment, recruited vs unrecruited SEPARATE (H9's falsifiable second clause preserved). CADENCE: weekly campaign, observational, working set only, non-evidential. RELATION TO THE PROPOSAL: the sign-propagation half of cascade-decay IS this organ on a denser rung set (densification, not new instrument); the per-event AGGREGATION-DECAY profile (one event's rv followed across simultaneous aggregations) is NOT currently measured anywhere — recruitment samples parent-bar rv at chain steps, not an event's rv survival across rungs. Half densification, half genuinely new organ.
